newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -- Moody's sees uncertain outlook in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -- Moody's sees uncertain outlook in Thailand.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said Thursday its outlook for Thailand was uncertain, as the agency watched how the Thai government would handle its economic problems.

Moody's analyst Vincent Truglia said the agency expected Thailand to respond "appropriately" to the instability and that the agency incorporated these response into the country's A3 foreign currency rating.
"It's an environment of heightened risk, however the expectation is that they will handle it appropriately," Trulia said.
"We'll have to closely monitor the policy reforms on the part of the government in the near term to see how the response actually works," Truglia said.
Truglia added that "inappropriate policy actions" to stem the financial instability could have a negative effect, even in the near term.
"We are in a period when the leeway is much more restricted, so that policy actions, if not appropriate, would have a greater impact," Truglia said.
Thai Finance Minister said Thursday that he would announce a major economic package within two weeks to help stabilize the volatile baht and bring down Thai interest rates.
The Thai baht slumped to fresh record low of 32.550/770 to the dollar Thursday amid ongoing pressure since the currency was set afloat from its basket July 2.

In a release, Moody's said that, although recent government policies should provide a minimal framework for the resolution of the country's economic difficulties, these measures may contribute to pressures in the financial sector with spillover effects on the balance of payments, the magnitude of which was too early to ascertain at present.
